headline: Healey pitches two-month gas-tax break as Massachusetts prices climb
dek: The governor says suspending the state's 24-cent-per-gallon tax would give drivers temporary relief, but the proposal still needs legislative approval and a funding plan.
body: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey is proposing a two-month suspension of the state's 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax, saying the temporary break would help families, truckers and rideshare drivers facing higher fuel costs.

Healey plans to include the measure in a supplemental spending bill. WBUR reported that the proposal carries an estimated $120 million price tag, which the administration says would be covered with surplus revenue from the state's surtax on household income above $1 million.

The announcement followed a campaign proposal from Republican gubernatorial candidate Michael Minogue, who has called for suspending the tax whenever gasoline rises above $4 a gallon and has backed eliminating it permanently. Healey's plan would last for a fixed two months rather than use a price trigger.

House Speaker Ron Mariano has called a suspension fiscally irresponsible, arguing that fuel-tax revenue supports transportation and infrastructure. Healey said the plan would not jeopardize transportation funding, but the proposal cannot take effect without approval from the Democrat-controlled Legislature.

The administration had not released all implementation details after Healey's announcement. Lawmakers will decide whether to include the tax break in the supplemental budget and how its cost would be covered.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Healey Proposes Two-Month Massachusetts Gas-Tax Suspension
seoDescription: Gov. Maura Healey proposed suspending Massachusetts' 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax for two months, a plan that needs legislative approval.
